key_insight: The paper shows that a quantum graph neural network can implement permutation-equivariant message passing and be positioned at a chosen Weisfeiler-Leman level, giving it a principled expressivity guarantee for graph learning.
engineering_relevance: This provides a scalable near-term quantum design for graph-structured problems, with pre-training and low-cost readout aimed at improving trainability and practical deployment.
method: Builds a quantum message-passing GNN that mirrors classical GNN structure.
Uses the Weisfeiler-Leman hierarchy to characterize and control graph distinguishability.
Trains first on smaller graph instances to support pre-training and scalability.
evidence_signal: The framework was tested in large-scale simulations up to 56 qubits across three datasets, including synthetic hard cases, molecular property prediction, and the travelling salesperson problem.
watch_item: Performance claims are based on simulation and model design; real hardware noise and circuit depth may affect scalability and readout fidelity.
paper_title: Scalable Message-Passing Quantum Graph Neural Networks in the Weisfeiler-Leman Hierarchy
